🇲🇽📈 <u>GUELAGUETZA 2026 BREAKS RECORDS: 278,000 TOURISTS, 1,138 MILLION PESOS</u>

The Guelaguetza in Oaxaca drew more than 278,000 national and foreign tourists and left a preliminary economic spillover of 1,138 million pesos between July 1 and 27 — up 1.43% from last year, El Economista reports.

The biggest indigenous festival in Mexico just posted its best year on record.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>DEA AND PENTAGON ADMIT TRUMP BOAT STRIKES DID NOT CUT DRUG SMUGGLING</u>

The same week Stephen Miller claims cartels control Mexican territory, US agencies blow up the pretext: the DEA found the deadly boat strikes in the Caribbean and the Pacific have not reduced drug smuggling into the US — cocaine supply and price untouched, routes diversified. 215 people killed for nothing.

The Mexican answer stands: cooperation yes, subordination no.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO KEEPS THE BEST TRADE TERMS WITH THE US — EBRARD</u>

Trump says he no longer cares about renewing the T-MEC. Yet his Section 301 tariff round hit 60 countries and left Mexico untouched — no new tariffs, same preferential frame.

“If you look at the overall picture of countries, Mexico has the best deal — which also explains why our exports to the United States have grown,” Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said, confirming the next negotiating round moves to Washington in early September. Integration is leverage.
banner: T-MEC: MEXICO KEEPS BEST US DEAL

🇲🇽🏠 <u>FOVISSSTE BUILDS HOUSING AGAIN AFTER 34 YEARS: 100,000 HOMES, 60 BILLION PESOS</u>

President Sheinbaum laid the first stone of the Fovissste Carmen Serdán housing complex in Puebla: a national goal of 100,000 homes with an initial investment of at least 60 billion pesos, plus credits in pesos with fixed payments for state workers earning up to two minimum wages.

For 34 years the housing fund of state workers built nothing. ISSSTE chief Martí Batres calls the return to construction part of a renacimiento of the institute — with medical clinics, SuperISSSTE stores and sports spaces included.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>AYOTZINAPA: NEW INVESTIGATIONS UNDERWAY, PARENTS OF THE 43 WILL BE INFORMED FIRST</u>

“There are new investigations and we are waiting to be able to give all the information to the mothers and fathers of Ayotzinapa,” President Sheinbaum announced, as the families asked the Supreme Court to halt a ruling that could close legal doors in the case.

Nearly 12 years after Iguala, the FGR and the national intelligence system keep working new lines of investigation. The case does not die.

🇲🇽🔬 <u>MEXICO BUILDS 58 NEW SEISMIC STATIONS, EXTENDS QUAKE MONITORING NATIONWIDE</u>

UNAM is expanding the Mexican Seismic Network with 58 new stations — 38 from the National Seismological Service and 20 from the Engineering Institute — reaching the least-instrumented north: Baja California, Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila and Nuevo León.

“There is the wrong perception that it does not shake there, but there is movement,” explains Leonardo Ramírez Guzmán, head of Seismic Engineering at UNAM. Mexico City already runs about 100 stations, on par with Tokyo and Los Angeles. The new stage, funded by the federal Security Ministry with CENAPRED, wraps up this year.

🌐🇲🇽 While the U.S. says “trade only with us,” Mexico just locked in Europe

On July 14 the EU Council gave final approval to the modernized EU-Mexico trade agreement, days after the European Parliament backed it 479–119. The deal removes almost all remaining tariffs between the two economies, saves European firms up to €100 million a year, and opens Mexican public procurement — with Mexico City targeting a 50% jump in exports to Europe by 2030.

The timing is the message. As Washington pressures Mexico to wall off Asia, Mexico is quietly multiplying its buyers: a ratified EU treaty, record trade across the Global South, and a seat at the multipolar table. Around 80% of exports still head north — which is exactly why every new market is insurance against coercion.

🌐 Diversification as strategy, not slogan: a country that can sell to more than one buyer can be threatened by none.

🔥🇲🇽🐉 Washington now wants Mexico to build a wall — around Chinese steel

In the July 24 USMCA talks in Mexico City, U.S. Trade Rep Jamieson Greer pressed Marcelo Ebrard to copy America's Section 232 tariff wall: 50% on core steel and aluminum from outside North America, 25% on derivatives — aimed squarely at China. The next round is set for September in Washington, with the U.S. wanting a framework deal closed by year's end.

The leverage they're counting on: the U.S. buys ~80% of Mexico's exports. But it cuts both ways. Mexico already taxes 1,463 product lines from countries with no trade deal (5–50%), and Beijing has formally branded those measures illegal barriers hitting $30B in Chinese exports. Adopting a U.S.-designed steel wall would hand Washington a veto over who Mexico may trade with.

🇲🇽 Sovereignty isn't choosing a master. It's refusing to let anyone — Beijing or Washington — write your tariff schedule for you.
